newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-STRIKER FASHANU UNCOMPROMISING OPPONENT ON PITCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STRIKER FASHANU UNCOMPROMISING OPPONENT ON PITCH.

text.p: Former England and Wimbledon striker John Fashanu shrugged off humble origins to make his name as a feared player on the soccer pitch and a successful businessman and television presenter off it.

The powerfully-built Fashanu, who goes on trial here on Tuesday charged with match-fixing, gained the nickname "Fash the Bash" after a series of violent clashes during games which left some opponents with serious injuries.

The striker, now 33, reached the peak of his fame at unfashionable south London club Wimbledon as part of the so-called "Crazy Gang" of players best known for their wild antics off the field and their tremendous team spirit.

He made two appearances for England in 1989, but made clear that soccer was only part of his life. His thriving business career helped him to riches and to become a role model for Britain's Afro-Caribbean community.

He is also a long-term presenter of a televised game show and acts as a special representative for the United Nations Children Fund (UNICEF) to Africa, where he specialises in boosting AIDS awareness.
But for all his success and good work away from soccer, his highly physical style meant controversy was never far away.
Within 15 minutes of his debut as a substitute for Wimbledon in 1986 he clashed with Portsmouth's Kevin Dillon, who suffered a broken jaw.

In 1987 he was involved in a tackle in a match against Norwich which led to Northern Ireland international John O'Neill's early retirement. O'Neill sued for damages and the case was eventually settled for a reported 70,000 pounds ($117,600).
The same year Fashanu hit a spectator at Everton after being spat on and was sent off after punching Queen Park Rangers' Martin Allen during a brawl.

In 1988 he helped Wimbledon win the F.A. Cup with a shock 1-0 victory over Liverpool, but he was also banned for three matches and fined 2,000 pounds for his part in an incident in a players' tunnel involving Manchester United's Viv Anderson.
In 1993 he was charged with misconduct by the Football Association after an incident in which Tottenham captain Gary Mabbutt suffered severe facial injuries, but was later cleared.
The same year he had a training ground bust-up with Wimbledon team mate Lawrie Sanchez, who said afterwards: "Fashanu used martial arts in a systematic attempt to damage my legs seriously."
In April 1994 he made a surprise 1.35 million pounds ($2.15 million) move to Aston Villa and scored on his league debut, but had to retire shortly afterwards with a knee injury.
After being abandoned by their Nigerian father, Fashanu and his elder brother Justin were brought up by foster parents in the eastern English country of Norfolk.
Justin was the first to make the grade as a soccer player, briefly rocketing to fame at local club Norwich, but he was eventually eclipsed by his brother.
It took John five years playing for Norwich, Lincoln and London side Millwall before he gained the attention of Wimbledon in 1986, for whom he made 324 appearances and scored 129 goals.
John Fashanu was born on September 18, 1963 in London. He is married to model Melissa Kassa-Mapsi. ($1=.5950 Pound)
